page.title: Release ladder
page.purpose: Let an operator schedule marketed deliverables, inspect transitive stream prerequisites, and see the goals whose priority follows the schedule.

priorities.statement: Which marketed deliverable ships at each rank
What must be true before a selected stream earns, including enabling work
Which goals will re-prioritize when a rank or derived urgency changes
Whether the ladder or goal source is unavailable, and why

states.description: The ladder and its prerequisite source are available.
The ladder is being read and its layout is reserved.
The ladder request succeeds but no marketed deliverables or stream prerequisites exist.
The ladder is readable but the goal source is unavailable; the missing source is named.
The ladder or goal source cannot be read; the source and reason remain visible.
The ladder request fails and the reason is stated.
Displayed ladder data is older than its freshness window and its age is visible.
The schedule, tree, and reverse impact rows remain readable in the mobile viewport.

elements.description: Ranked marketed deliverables with class and finish bar.
Selects the revenue stream whose prerequisites are shown.
Indented prerequisite rows with depth, status, class, finish bar, and urgency.
Goals affected by a deliverable rank or urgency change.
Names an unavailable source and its reason.

claims.statement: Each reached prerequisite shows its depth, class, finish bar, status, and derived urgency.
The reverse view lists goals that re-prioritize when a deliverable's urgency changes.
An unavailable source is named with its reason rather than rendered as an empty result.
The release ladder exposes its schedule and impact regions in the mobile state.
